learn: Regular activity strengthens the heart, lungs, bones and muscles.
It improves mood, sleep, focus and self-confidence.
Habits formed now often last into adulthood.
lessons.try: List five benefits of fitness that matter most to you.

learn: Teens need 60 minutes of moderate-to-vigorous activity daily.
Include muscle- and bone-strengthening at least three days a week.
Reduce long periods of sitting and screen time.
check: Teens need ___ minutes of activity daily.
Muscle strengthening is recommended ___ days a week.
lessons.try: Log your activity for a week and compare it to guidelines.

learn: Common barriers: time, cost, access, motivation.
Solutions: short workouts, free activities, friends, scheduling.
Small changes add up.
lessons.try: Identify your top barrier and plan a solution.

learn: The PACER or 1-mile run measures aerobic fitness.
Resting heart rate is often 60-100 bpm; lower can mean better fitness.
Estimated max heart rate is about 220 minus age.
check: Estimated max heart rate for a 17-year-old is...
Resting heart rate is often ___ bpm.
lessons.try: Measure your resting heart rate three mornings in a row.

learn: Push-ups, curl-ups and plank holds test muscular endurance.
The sit-and-reach tests hamstring and lower back flexibility.
Use correct form for valid results.
lessons.try: Complete strength and flexibility tests and record results.

learn: Compare results to healthy fitness zones, not to others.
Identify strengths and areas for growth.
Use results to set goals.
check: A fitness profile shows strengths and...
lessons.try: Write a fitness profile from your test results.

learn: Moderate intensity is about 64-76% of max heart rate; vigorous is about 77-93%.
The talk test: moderate lets you talk; vigorous makes talking hard.
Monitor heart rate with a pulse check or tracker.
check: At 70% of a 200 bpm max, the target is...
lessons.try: Calculate your target heart rate zone.

learn: Continuous training: steady effort for 20 minutes or more.
Interval training alternates hard and easy efforts.
Fartlek mixes speeds freely during a run.
lessons.try: Complete an interval workout and record heart rate.

learn: Cross-training uses different activities (swim, cycle, row) to reduce overuse injuries.
It keeps training interesting.
Choose low-impact options when recovering.
lessons.try: Plan a week of cross-training.

learn: Resistance training uses body weight, bands or weights to build strength.
Sets and repetitions: 8-12 reps for general strength and endurance.
Rest 48 hours before working the same muscles hard again.
check: A common rep range for general strength is...
Rest about ___ hours before working the same muscles hard.
Body weight can be used as...
lessons.try: Learn five body-weight exercises with correct form.

learn: Warm up first; use controlled movements.
Breathe out during effort and in during the return.
Use a spotter for heavy lifts and start light.
lessons.try: Practise squats and push-ups with feedback on form.

learn: Major groups: chest, back, shoulders, arms, core, glutes and legs.
Balance pushing and pulling exercises.
Train the whole body, not just favourite areas.
lessons.try: Design a full-body routine with one exercise per group.

learn: Dynamic stretching (leg swings) suits warm-ups.
Static stretching (hold 15-30 seconds) suits cool-downs.
Never bounce or stretch into pain.
lessons.try: Lead a five-minute cool-down stretch routine.

learn: Mobility is moving joints through their full range with control.
Good posture reduces back and neck pain.
Breaks from sitting protect your spine.
check: Mobility is range of motion with...
lessons.try: Check your posture at a desk and adjust your set-up.

learn: Balance relies on the core, inner ear and vision.
Yoga and tai chi improve balance and focus.
Balance training reduces falls and injuries.
lessons.try: Try a beginner yoga or tai chi sequence.

learn: Choose frequency, intensity, time and type for each component.
Base the plan on your fitness test results and goals.
Include warm-ups, cool-downs and rest days.
lessons.try: Draft a four-week plan.

learn: Increase load gradually (about 10% a week).
Track workouts in a log or app.
Adjust when progress stalls.
check: Progress gradually by about ___ a week.
lessons.try: Keep a training log for four weeks.

learn: Re-test at the end of the plan.
Reflect on what worked and what didn't.
Set new goals for the next cycle.
check: Re-test at the ___ of the plan.
lessons.try: Re-test and write a reflection.

learn: Eat a carbohydrate-rich meal 2-4 hours before exercise.
After exercise, combine carbohydrates and protein to recover.
Whole foods beat supplements for most teens.
check: Eat a pre-exercise meal about ___ hours before.
Most teens are best served by...
lessons.try: Plan pre- and post-game meals.

learn: Drink before, during and after exercise.
Weigh before and after practice to estimate fluid loss.
Watch for heat exhaustion: heavy sweating, dizziness, nausea.
check: Weight lost in practice is mostly...
lessons.try: Make a hydration plan for a hot-weather practice.

learn: Many supplements are untested and unregulated.
Performance-enhancing drugs are banned and dangerous.
Ask a doctor or dietitian before taking any supplement.
lessons.try: Evaluate claims in a supplement advertisement.

learn: Muscles rebuild during rest, not during the workout.
Sleep is the most important recovery tool.
Active recovery (light walking, swimming) aids healing.
check: The most important recovery tool is...
lessons.try: Plan a recovery day.

learn: Signs: persistent fatigue, poor performance, irritability, frequent illness.
Overtraining needs rest and reduced training.
Balance training with life and school.
lessons.try: Review your schedule for overtraining risk.

learn: Sprains (ligaments), strains (muscles), fractures (bones), concussions (brain).
Concussion signs: headache, confusion, dizziness; stop playing and see a doctor.
Return to play only with medical clearance.
check: After a suspected concussion you should...
lessons.try: Make a concussion awareness poster.

learn: Exercise releases endorphins and improves mood.
It reduces anxiety and symptoms of depression.
It improves memory and concentration.
lessons.try: Rate your mood before and after a workout for a week.

learn: Mindful movement focuses attention on breath and body.
Yoga, walking meditation and stretching calm the nervous system.
Even five minutes helps.
lessons.try: Practise a mindful walk outdoors.

learn: Healthy body image values what your body can do.
Media images are often edited.
Disordered eating is serious; tell a trusted adult or doctor if worried.
check: If worried about disordered eating, tell a...
lessons.try: Write about three things your body lets you do.

learn: Choose activities you enjoy: hiking, dance, cycling, swimming, martial arts, team leagues.
Variety prevents boredom.
Activity can be social.
lessons.try: Try a new lifelong activity this month.

learn: Parks, rec centres, community colleges and clubs offer activities.
Many are free or low-cost.
Workplaces may offer wellness programmes.
lessons.try: Map three activity resources near you.

learn: Plan for changes in schedule, job and family.
Keep activity a priority with short, regular sessions.
Health is a lifelong investment.
check: Short regular sessions keep activity a...
lessons.try: Write a five-year activity plan.
